```{r setup, include=FALSE}
source("../../_shared/template/viscount_rmd_helpers.R")

sett_raw <- jsonlite::fromJSON("modern_southern_africa_settlements.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)
summary_cache <- jsonlite::fromJSON("modern_southern_africa_summary_cache.json", simplifyVector = FALSE)

all_keys <- names(sett_raw)
all_entries <- lapply(all_keys, function (k) {
  e <- sett_raw[[k]]
  e$key <- k
  ps <- as.numeric(unlist(e$population))
  e$peak_pop_val <- if (length(ps) > 0L) max(ps) else 0
  e
})

iso3_map <- c(
  "Angola" = "AGO",
  "Botswana" = "BWA",
  "Lesotho" = "LSO",
  "Mozambique" = "MOZ",
  "Namibia" = "NAM",
  "South Africa" = "ZAF",
  "Zambia" = "ZMB",
  "Zimbabwe" = "ZWE",
  "eSwatini" = "SWZ"
)

fmt_eu_coord <- function (x) {
  s <- format(round(as.numeric(x), 2L), nsmall = 2L, trim = TRUE)
  gsub("\\.", ",", s)
}

fmt_era_yr <- function (y) {
  paste0(as.integer(y), "AD")
}

interp_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  ord <- order(yrs)
  yrs <- yrs[ord]
  vals <- vals[ord]
  if (yr_num < yrs[1] || yr_num > yrs[length(yrs)]) return(NA_real_)
  idx <- which(yrs == yr_num)
  if (length(idx) > 0L) return(vals[idx[1]])
  stats::approx(x = yrs, y = vals, xout = yr_num, method = "linear")$y
}

fmt_site_pop <- function (e, yr_num) {
  p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr_num)
  if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) return("-")
  viscount_fmt_pop(p)
}

fmt_site_peak <- function (e) {
  ps <- e$population
  if (is.null(ps) || length(ps) == 0L) return("-")
  yrs <- as.numeric(names(ps))
  vals <- as.numeric(unlist(ps))
  i_pk <- which.max(vals)
  paste0(viscount_fmt_pop(vals[i_pk]), " (", fmt_era_yr(yrs[i_pk]), ")")
}

sort_entries <- function (sub_list) {
  pks <- vapply(sub_list, function (e) e$peak_pop_val, numeric(1))
  nms <- vapply(sub_list, function (e) as.character(e$name), character(1))
  sub_list[order(-pks, nms)]
}

zaf_all <- Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), "South Africa"), all_entries)
zaf_t1 <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) e$peak_pop_val >= 100000, zaf_all))
zaf_t2 <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) e$peak_pop_val >= 30000 && e$peak_pop_val < 100000, zaf_all))
zaf_t3 <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) e$peak_pop_val >= 15000 && e$peak_pop_val < 30000, zaf_all))
zaf_t4 <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) e$peak_pop_val >= 8000 && e$peak_pop_val < 15000, zaf_all))
zaf_t5 <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) e$peak_pop_val < 8000, zaf_all))

nam_entries <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), "Namibia"), all_entries))
bwa_entries <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), "Botswana"), all_entries))
lso_entries <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), "Lesotho"), all_entries))
swz_entries <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) identical(as.character(e$country), "eSwatini"), all_entries))
buf_entries <- sort_entries(Filter(function (e) !(as.character(e$country) %in% c("South Africa", "Namibia", "Botswana", "Lesotho", "eSwatini")), all_entries))

build_gazetteer_df <- function (sub_list) {
  rows <- lapply(sub_list, function (e) {
    iso_code <- iso3_map[[as.character(e$country)]]
    if (is.null(iso_code)) iso_code <- toupper(substr(as.character(e$country), 1L, 3L))
    loc_str <- paste0(iso_code, ": ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[1]]), ", ", fmt_eu_coord(e$coords[[2]]))
    nm <- as.character(e$name)
    if (identical(nm, "(no name)")) nm <- "Unnamed Sekhukhune Locality"
    sc <- if (identical(as.character(e$population_scope), "metro")) "Metro" else "City"
    data.frame(
      Settlement = nm,
      Scope = sc,
      Location = loc_str,
      `1910AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1910),
      `1952AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1952),
      `1970AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1970),
      `1995AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 1995),
      `2025AD` = fmt_site_pop(e, 2025),
      Peak = fmt_site_peak(e),
      check.names = FALSE,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  })
  df <- do.call(rbind, rows)
  rownames(df) <- NULL
  df
}

n_excluded <- as.integer(summary_cache$wave_saturation_stats$ledger_excluded)
n_candidates <- length(all_entries) + n_excluded
bench_nums <- c(1910, 1952, 1970, 1995, 2025)
bench_keys <- as.character(bench_nums)
n_active <- setNames(
  vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) sum(vapply(all_entries, function (e) !is.na(interp_site_pop(e, yr)), logical(1))), integer(1)),
  bench_keys
)

group_list <- list(
  list(label = "South Africa: Tier 1 (>= 100k Peak)", entries = zaf_t1),
  list(label = "South Africa: Tier 2 (30k to < 100k Peak)", entries = zaf_t2),
  list(label = "South Africa: Tier 3 (15k to < 30k Peak)", entries = zaf_t3),
  list(label = "South Africa: Tier 4 (8k to < 15k Peak)", entries = zaf_t4),
  list(label = "South Africa: Tier 5 (< 8k Peak)", entries = zaf_t5),
  list(label = "Namibia", entries = nam_entries),
  list(label = "Botswana", entries = bwa_entries),
  list(label = "Lesotho", entries = lso_entries),
  list(label = "Eswatini", entries = swz_entries),
  list(label = "Cross-Border Buffer (MOZ, AGO, ZMB, ZWE)", entries = buf_entries)
)
```

# Abstract

This gazetteer compiles coordinates, spatial scopes and multi-period population series for `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` individually assessed urban and rural settlements across Modern Southern Africa between 1902AD and 2026AD. Screened from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_candidates, 0L)` candidate places (`r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate alias records and overlapping boundary shells excluded), the retained entries span `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` chronological observations across South Africa (1.232), Namibia (94), Botswana (70), Lesotho (48), Eswatini (33) and 22 cross-border buffer towns in Mozambique, Angola, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Active interpolated entries rise from `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1910"]], 0L)` centres in 1910AD to `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1952"]], 0L)` in 1952AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1970"]], 0L)` in 1970AD, `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["1995"]], 0L)` in 1995AD and `r viscount_fmt_number(n_active[["2025"]], 0L)` by 2025AD, led by the metropolitan agglomerations of Johannesburg (11,01M), Cape Town (4,39M), Durban (3,52M), Maputo (2,98M), Windhoek (566,2k), Gaborone (534,8k), Maseru (505,7k) and Manzini (328,9k).

```{r fig1-md-only, results='asis'}
    "figures/fig_01_map.png",
    "Spatial distribution of 1.499 assessed settlements across Modern Southern Africa from 1902AD to 2026AD.",
    "fig:hero-settlements-southern-africa"
  )
}
```

# Background

Compiling a unified twentieth- and early twenty-first-century settlement gazetteer for Southern Africa requires reconciling disparate colonial, Apartheid and post-colonial enumeration traditions [@Caldwell2002HistoricalPopulation; @ChimereDan2013ApartheidAnd]. Union and Republic censuses in South Africa separated European municipal boroughs from segregated townships and ethnic Bantustans between 1911AD and 1991AD, whereas post-1994AD wall-to-wall municipalities merged suburban cores and outlying settlements into single metropolitan jurisdictions [@Simkins2011SouthAfrica; @Bakker2020MigrationAnd]. Neighbouring statistical agencies in Namibia, Botswana, Lesotho and Eswatini similarly transitioned from colonial district headcounts to modern geocoded village and town registers [@StatsSA2023Census2022; @NSA2024NamibiaCensus; @StatsBotswana2022Census].

# Methodology

## Candidate Screening and Territorial Accounting

Candidate settlements were screened from official census tables, OECD/SWAC Africapolis urban polygons, UNSD Demographic Yearbook series and historical statistical registers [@StatsSA2023Census2022; @Deleu2015ImprovingAfripop]. Across the `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$total_area_km2, 0L)` km² study domain bounded over geoBoundaries administrative outlines [@Runfola2020GeoBoundaries], `r viscount_fmt_number(n_excluded, 0L)` duplicate alias records were removed, leaving `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` retained settlements across `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations. Of those entries, 1.477 fall inside the five core sovereign territories (1.487 interior cell matches across the 46 Admin-1 sub-regions plus coastal or frontier edge matches) and 22 lie in adjacent border corridors of Mozambique, Angola, Zambia and Zimbabwe to anchor cross-frontier interpolation.

## Scope Classification and Benchmark Interpolation

Every settlement carries an explicit spatial scope distinguishing `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$city_proper, 0L)` city-proper places from `r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$metro, 0L)` metropolitan agglomerations, preventing municipal cores and encompassing urban footprints from being conflated [@Bakker2020MigrationAnd]. Tables \ref{tab:zaf-t1} through \ref{tab:buf-sites} list all 1.499 settlements partitioned by country and South African peak-population tier, reporting linearly interpolated populations at 1910AD, 1952AD, 1970AD, 1995AD and 2025AD alongside each settlement's observed peak population and peak year. Dates preceding foundation or earliest census attestation and dates after municipal absorption or boundary discontinuation appear as hyphens (-).

# Testing and Validation

Across all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements, rank-size regression yields $q = 0,98$ ($R^2 = 0,9922$) across the upper 180 urban centres and $q = 1,40$ ($R^2 = 0,8893$) across the full ledger, matching the 1.414 spatially deduplicated settlement peaks ($q = 0,99$, $R^2 = 0,99$) plotted in Figure \ref{fig:settlements-rank}. Chronological and coordinate screening eliminates duplicate urban synonyms and checks alignment between historical boundary transitions and municipal census dates [@Udjo2014EstimatingDemographic; @Mkhatha2024ResponseMoultrie].

```{r fig3-ranksize, results='asis'}
viscount_figure(
  "figures/fig_03_rank_size.png",
  "Zipf rank-size curve across 1.414 deduplicated peaks (q = 0,99, R² = 0,99) and ten densest sub-regions in 2025AD.",
  "fig:settlements-rank",
  arg3_options = list(max_height = "0.38\\textheight")
)
```

# Results

## South Africa: Tier 1 Metropolitan Agglomerations and Major Cities (92 Sites)

Table \ref{tab:zaf-t1} records the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(zaf_t1), 0L)` largest South African centres reaching 100k or more inhabitants at peak, led by the Johannesburg agglomeration (11,01M), Cape Town agglomeration (4,39M), Durban agglomeration (3,52M), Soshanguve (1,91M), Pretoria agglomeration (1,76M), Evaton (1,09M) and Port Elizabeth (957,3k) [@StatsSA2023Census2022; @Simkins2011SouthAfrica].

```{r tab-zaf-t1, results='asis'}
viscount_table(
  build_gazetteer_df(zaf_t1),
  "South African settlements reaching 100k or more inhabitants at peak (1910AD to 2025AD).",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:zaf-t1", font_size = "scriptsize")
)
```

# Limitations

Three caveats govern this settlement ledger. First, individual place series terminate or shift scope when municipal boundaries are amalgamated, meaning pre-2000AD city-proper entries and post-2000AD metropolitan agglomerations appear as separate rows to prevent artificial leaps [@Bakker2020MigrationAnd]. Second, interpolated benchmark columns display a hyphen outside each settlement's attested span, so settlements founded after 1952AD (such as Gaborone in 1964AD or Secunda in the 1970s) show blanks at earlier benchmarks. Third, summing raw rows across both city-proper and metropolitan entries double-counts overlapping urban cores and should never substitute for the 46-polygon regional totals in the companion literature review.

# Conclusion

Together, the `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements catalogued in Tables \ref{tab:zaf-t1} through \ref{tab:buf-sites} trace Southern Africa's urban transformation from 1902AD colonial mining and port nodes to contemporary metropolitan corridors, anchoring both sub-national disaggregation and rank-size calibration across all five sovereign states.

# Appendix

## Gazetteer Summary by Country and Regional Tier

Table \ref{tab:gazetteer-summary} reconciles site counts, city-proper versus metropolitan scopes, chronological observations and combined unadjusted interpolated sums across every country and South African size tier, accounting for all `r viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L)` settlements (`r viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L)` observations).

```{r tab-appendix-summary, results='asis'}
sum_rows <- lapply(group_list, function (grp) {
  sub <- grp$entries
  n_city <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) identical(as.character(e$population_scope), "city_proper"), logical(1)))
  n_met <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) identical(as.character(e$population_scope), "metro"), logical(1)))
  n_obs <- sum(vapply(sub, function (e) length(e$population), integer(1)))
  sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
    vals <- vapply(sub, function (e) {
      p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
      if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
    }, numeric(1))
    viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
  }, character(1)), bench_keys)
  data.frame(
    Group = grp$label,
    Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(sub), 0L),
    `City/Metro` = paste0(viscount_fmt_number(n_city, 0L), "/", viscount_fmt_number(n_met, 0L)),
    Obs = viscount_fmt_number(n_obs, 0L),
    `1910AD` = sums[["1910"]],
    `1952AD` = sums[["1952"]],
    `1970AD` = sums[["1970"]],
    `1995AD` = sums[["1995"]],
    `2025AD` = sums[["2025"]],
    check.names = FALSE,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
})
tot_sums <- setNames(vapply(bench_nums, function (yr) {
  vals <- vapply(all_entries, function (e) {
    p <- interp_site_pop(e, yr)
    if (is.na(p) || p <= 0) 0 else p
  }, numeric(1))
  viscount_fmt_pop(sum(vals))
}, character(1)), bench_keys)
tot_row <- data.frame(
  Group = "All Ledger Entries",
  Sites = viscount_fmt_number(length(all_entries), 0L),
  `City/Metro` = paste0(
    viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$city_proper, 0L),
    "/",
    viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$population_scope_counts$metro, 0L)
  ),
  Obs = viscount_fmt_number(summary_cache$observation_count, 0L),
  `1910AD` = tot_sums[["1910"]],
  `1952AD` = tot_sums[["1952"]],
  `1970AD` = tot_sums[["1970"]],
  `1995AD` = tot_sums[["1995"]],
  `2025AD` = tot_sums[["2025"]],
  check.names = FALSE,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
df_sum <- rbind(do.call(rbind, sum_rows), tot_row)
rownames(df_sum) <- NULL
viscount_table(
  df_sum,
  "Summary of assessed settlement counts, spatial scopes, chronological observations and combined interpolated site totals by country and tier.",
  arg3_options = list(label = "tab:gazetteer-summary")
)
```

# Footnotes

Linear interpolation is bounded strictly between each settlement's earliest and latest attested census or Africapolis observations; one unnamed Sekhukhune locality in the source Africapolis feed is labelled Unnamed Sekhukhune Locality in Table \ref{tab:zaf-t3}.
